name: Rosling Bubble Trails
summary: Gapminder-style bubbles and trails under a giant watermark clock; the checkout bubble sinks at 09:42.
look: White stage, pale L-axes and faint grid, translucent bubbles with thin ink outlines and dotted ghost trails. A huge pale watermark clock behind everything; Pulse is a big teal bubble, the anomaly a coral one.

components.name: Metric bubble
components.role: translucent circle, size = volume, one per metric

components.name: Ghost trail
components.role: fading echoes + dotted path of where a bubble has been

components.name: Watermark clock
components.role: giant pale timestamp behind the chart that tells the time

components.name: Pulse bubble
components.role: the big teal bubble that everything else orbits

components.name: Axis frame
components.role: L-shaped axis with mono labels, faint grid

components.name: Decision strip
components.role: rule + −18% + context + Roll back, below the chart

motion.name: Bubble drift
motion.how: positions interpolate linearly between keyframes every beat (0.5 s at 120 BPM) for the Gapminder 'play' feel

motion.name: Trail echo
motion.how: each 0.25 s a ghost copy is left behind at 30 % opacity and fades over 1 bar

motion.name: Clock roll
motion.how: watermark digits change on every downbeat, 2-frame crossfade; freeze + 1.03 scale bump on the anomaly

story: Hook: grey bubbles drift under a FRI watermark while a coral one is only found Monday. Drop: every bubble is pulled into the big teal Pulse bubble. Proof: the Checkout bubble sinks with a trail at 09:42 after deploy #2231, −18%, Roll back. CTA: the bubble climbs back to the trend by 09:48, Caught before customers noticed., Start free.
adapt: Plot your product's entities (accounts, services, campaigns) on two axes that matter to your users, size by volume, and let your anomaly be one bubble that breaks away with a trail.

references.note: Gapminder's animated bubble chart: x, y, size, colour and time
Rosling's TED talk that made animated bubbles famous

fit.risk: Scatter axes need a second of reading; label the one bubble that matters and keep the rest unlabelled or dim.
